_**Agent (2026-08-04 05:41:13Z)**_

Yes—we shipped an official stable `v0.8.0` release.

- Public, non-draft, non-prerelease: [DeadReckon v0.8.0](https://github.com/gregce/deadreckon/releases/tag/v0.8.0)
- Published August 3, 2026
- Tag resolves to commit `5a42d6f40f1f8ccb02ec1cf69d91a3a6cd31dbe7`
- [Release workflow](https://github.com/gregce/deadreckon/actions/runs/30818860986) completed successfully
- 22 public assets, including five platform archives, installers, checksums, SBOM, attestations, and trust evidence
- Homebrew formula is live at version `0.8.0`
- npm was intentionally deferred
- Windows signing was intentionally deferred

One caveat: we subsequently discovered incorrect macOS signing/notarization fields in the public `release-manifest.json`. The actual macOS binaries were signed and notarized, but the manifest’s metadata was wrong due to trust-file discovery. That defect is fixed on `main`, after the `v0.8.0` tag, so it would be included in a future patch release.

The current local tree is dirty only with unrelated SpecStory records and generated directories; that does not affect the published tag.

_**Agent (2026-08-04 05:41:13Z)**_

The recorded failure rules out timing as the root cause of this particular stop: Codex reached `turn.started` and immediately returned HTTP 400 for an invalid response schema. But timing is implicated in the separate supervisor identity warning, and the authoring pipeline has several fixed allocations that deserve an end-to-end audit.

I’ll therefore test phase boundaries by behavior—startup readiness, draft, critic, redraft, provider cleanup, and handoff—and relax only deadlines that can reject healthy progress. Hard no-progress and cleanup bounds will remain, because removing them would recreate the indefinite-run failures we just fixed.

_**Agent (2026-08-04 05:41:13Z)**_

The closest working sibling is the semantic-judge schema: it uses fixed object properties and arrays, never an object with arbitrary property names. The broken done-authoring schema is the outlier: its `files` field is a free-form object map. I’m now running a minimal real Codex discrimination test—same model and strict schema mode, but comparing a fixed `files` field with the dynamic map—before changing anything.

_**Agent (2026-08-04 05:41:13Z)**_

Diagnosis is now pinned down:

- `start` correctly chose the selected Campaign planner (`cli:codex / gpt-5.6-sol`) after commit `d2c087e`; the default-provider selection is not the fault.
- DeadReckon’s built-in draft schema in `commands/acceptance.rs` defines `files` as an arbitrary-key object. The Codex adapter writes that schema verbatim and invokes strict `--output-schema`.
- A real A/B test against the installed Codex `0.146.0` proved the boundary: the same root schema works when `files` is fixed-shape, fails immediately when it is a dynamic map, and works when helper files are represented as an array of `{path, contents}`.
- Existing tests accidentally canonized the invalid schema and used fake CLIs that never validate it.
- The deprecation warning is also ours: DeadReckon always passes `--disable web_search_request` even after Codex reports that feature as deprecated.
- The bad recovery hint is a separate code defect: every authoring error is mapped to the same `config set defaults.doc_provider cli:codex` command, even when the selected Codex route just failed.
- The supervisor warning is another independent defect: macOS boot identity stores the entire `kern.boottime` string and compares volatile microseconds exactly. Your two values had the same boot second but different microseconds.
- Timing did not cause the HTTP 400, but this flow has brittle phase caps: 30 seconds for CLI course planning, 5 seconds for service readiness, and effective 57/17/57-second draft/critic/redraft windows.

I’ll fix the protocol shape and provider capability handling first, prove them, and push that commit. Then I’ll address boot identity, recovery affordances, and progress-tolerant phase timing as a second independently testable commit.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-04 05:48:05Z)**_

Read-only audit complete; I made no edits.

## Phase trace

Guided start currently flows through:

1. Source selection and Git validation.
2. Optional goal-shape planner.
3. Mode, provider, model and team selection.
4. Done-contract draft, critic and optional redraft.
5. Human contract review and final launch confirmation.
6. Supervisor preflight, installation/restart and readiness.
7. Contract/source/gate freezing and Job queueing.
8. Detached supervisor spawn.
9. Lease claim and launch-input validation.
10. `ChildLaunchPrepared`, then `AttemptStarted`.
11. Guarded launcher acknowledgement and a second launch-input validation.
12. Driver source/worktree setup.
13. First persisted Run state.
14. For Graph/Campaign: root planner, durable Plan/Campaign, then child Run states.

Human pauses are correctly unbounded. Job wall time begins at `AttemptStarted`; pre-admission and supervisor setup do not consume it. An absolute `--deadline`, however, keeps advancing throughout the entire process.

## What recent main changes improved

Commit `f3a97fb` substantially improved the common case:

- Shape planning: CLI `30s → 60s`, HTTP `5s → 15s`, with `30s` cleanup.
- Contract authoring: default `120s → 600s`, clamp `300–3,600s`, stage caps `300/120/300s`, cleanup `10s`.
- Supervisor readiness: `5s → 30s`.
- Lease TTL: `15s → 60s`; heartbeat remains `2s`.
- Guarded-child settlement: `2s → 30s`.
- launchd bootstrap transition: six retries totaling `5.85s`.
- macOS boot identity now ignores volatile microseconds.

These are sensible relaxations, but four boundary defects remain.

## Release-blocking findings

1. Unreaped shape planner does not stop admission.

At [start.rs:545](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/start.rs:545), a timeout whose cleanup cannot be proven warns and returns `None`. `None` also means “use the deterministic course,” so DeadReckon continues into contract authoring while the earlier provider may still be alive.

Change the result to distinguish:

- deterministic fallback after proven cleanup;
- provider unavailable;
- unresolved provider process, which must fail closed.

Test: a fake planner ignores cancellation; assert no contract provider starts, no Job is created, and the PID record remains.

2. A live same-boot lease is still reclaimed after 60 seconds.

At [job_lease.rs:144](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/job_lease.rs:144), expiry is checked without confirming whether the same-boot owner process is still the same live process. After a machine sleeps for over 60 seconds, a second supervisor can reclaim the lease as soon as both wake.

The documentation claim that the new TTL prevents host sleep from reclaiming a healthy owner is therefore false.

The robust fix is to bind leases to process-start identity and reclaim an expired same-boot lease only when that exact owner is dead. Tests should cover:

- live same-boot owner beyond TTL: no reclaim;
- dead exact owner: reclaim;
- different boot: immediate reclaim;
- reused PID: reclaim safely.

3. Admission can queue an already-expired Job.

`create_job` validates wall/spend/attempt limits but not deadline freshness at [job.rs:139](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/job.rs:139). Contract authoring, operator review, service repair and source hashing may consume the absolute deadline; the Job is then queued and immediately terminalized.

Check the deadline again at the final queue boundary, after expensive freezing/hashing and before durable `job.json`/events. A past deadline should refuse without leaving a Job.

Tests:

- past deadline creates no Job;
- deadline crossing during injected admission delay creates no Job;
- a still-future deadline is preserved exactly, not extended.

4. Stored-plan replay has the old phase order.

Ordinary start materializes the contract before supervisor mutation at [start.rs:3991](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/start.rs:3991). Replay still starts/repairs the supervisor first, then materializes the contract at [start.rs:3886](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/start.rs:3886).

Reorder replay to match ordinary start. Test that failed replay authoring does not invoke service setup.

## Important next fixes

- Service-manager commands are unbounded. The `30s` readiness timer begins only after synchronous `launchctl`/`systemctl` calls return. `run_required` and `run_observational` use unrestricted `Command::output()` in `supervisor_service.rs`. Give each command a bounded, process-reaped execution path and make the setup allowance cover commands plus readiness.

- Contract stages can starve later stages. Allocation is simply `min(remaining, stage_cap)`. With a configured `300s` budget, the draft can consume all 300 seconds, leaving no critic. Even the `600s` default is smaller than `300 + 120 + 300`. Reserve minimum critic/redraft capacity or revise the allocation model; test with paused time.

- Detached handoff is not proven. [job.rs:365](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/job.rs:365) reports “in flight” after process spawn, before lease acquisition or any child state. Either call this “queued” or add a bounded acknowledgement that the Job was leased, while preserving detached behavior.

- First-state failures remain a blind spot. Worktree preparation at [run.rs:850](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/run.rs:850) occurs before `create_run` at [run.rs:961](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/run.rs:961). The current `LegacyUnknown` correction is more truthful than blaming the provider, but a durable bootstrap record would allow typed blocked/configuration outcomes and safe recovery.

- Launch inputs are validated once before `AttemptStarted` and again inside the guarded launcher after it. The second source-tree hash consumes Job wall time before Run state exists. A post-validation launcher acknowledgement or explicit bootstrap phase would remove that ambiguity.

- The lease heartbeat thread exits on its first heartbeat error, but the supervising task does not learn that until guard drop. It should report failure promptly, retry within a bounded window, or stop the owned tree before lease expiry.

- The Graph root planner at [plan.rs:846](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/plan.rs:846) has no phase timeout, cancellation token or PID record; it is bounded only by the entire Job wall/deadline. This is not too short, but a stalled planner can consume the full default 10-hour Job allowance before any Plan exists.

## Documentation corrections

[AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md) still contains the obsolete `120s`, `30–600s`, `60/20/60s` authoring description, alongside the newer `600s` description. It also overstates the protection against host-sleep lease reclaim. Both should be corrected before `v0.8.1`.
